ai.issueType: Heading permalink aria-label excludes visible hash symbol
ai.description: The anchor link displays a visible "#" character (line 1360) but the aria-label set on line 1358 is "Link to section: {heading text}", which does not contain the "#" symbol. Speech input users who see the "#" and say "click hash" or "click number" will fail to activate the link because the accessible name lacks that text, violating SC 2.5.3 Label in Name.

ai.issueType: Cart counter update not announced to screen readers
ai.description: When users click an element with the data-add-cart attribute, the cart counter text content is updated dynamically to reflect the new count, but the change is not announced via the available announce() function. Screen reader users receive no feedback that an item has been added to the cart or that the cart count has changed.

ai.issueType: Form validation errors not associated with inputs via aria-describedby
ai.description: When a form field fails validation, the code creates an error message element with a unique ID and sets aria-invalid="true" on the input, but it fails to add aria-describedby to the input element referencing the error message ID. Screen reader users cannot associate the displayed error message with the specific form field that needs correction.

ai.issueType: Live region role configured after content update in newsletter announcement
ai.description: In the showState function, the status message textContent is updated before the element's live region role (alert or status) is set. When the element becomes visible, screen readers may fail to announce the message because the live region was not active when the text was inserted, reducing the effectiveness of the status announcement.

ai.issueType: Bookmark list live region recreated on every update
ai.description: The `renderList` function replaces the container's innerHTML including the `<ul>` element that has `aria-live="polite"`. When a live region element is destroyed and recreated during content updates, screen readers may fail to announce changes because the live region was not present in the DOM before the content changed. This affects users relying on screen readers to be notified when bookmarks are added or removed.

ai.issueType: Preference change announcement uses internal key instead of human-readable label
ai.description: When a preference input changes, the CosmosAnnouncer announces "Preference saved: " followed by the internal preference key (e.g., "fontSize", "lineSpacing", "dyslexicFont"). Screen reader users hear technical property names rather than human-readable labels (e.g., "Font size", "Line spacing"), which may be confusing or unclear, particularly for users with cognitive disabilities or those unfamiliar with technical terminology.

ai.issueType: Router navigation does not update document title
ai.description: The single-page application router updates the browser history and announces navigation to screen readers, but it never updates the document title. Screen reader users rely on the page title to understand the current context; without updates, the title remains stale and does not reflect the current route's content, violating WCAG 2.4.2.

ai.issueType: Preference cycle buttons missing click handler implementation
ai.description: The code sets up elements with [data-pref-cycle] as custom buttons (role="button", tabindex="0") and adds keyboard support (Enter/Space triggers click), but no click event listener is registered for these elements within the provided code. Mouse users clicking these elements will experience no action, and keyboard users triggering the click event via Enter/Space will also experience no action because the handler is missing. This violates WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard and 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value as the buttons have role and keyboard support but lack the actual functionality.

ai.issueType: Theme toggle buttons may lack accessible names depending on DOM content
ai.description: The JavaScript enhances elements to be buttons but does not ensure they have accessible names. If the HTML markup for [data-theme-toggle] elements contains only icon characters (☀, ☾, ⊙) inserted at line 720 without accompanying aria-label or visible text, screen reader users will hear the icon character (which may be read as "sun", "moon", or "circle with dot" depending on the screen reader) without context that these are theme controls. This violates WCAG 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) and 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value.

ai.issueType: Bootstrap task error handling swallows non-critical errors without user notification
ai.description: When a non-critical bootstrap task fails, the error is logged to the console but not announced to screen reader users via a live region. Users relying on assistive technologies may experience a partially broken interface without knowing that some functionality failed to initialize, violating WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages.

ai.issueType: Dropdown setup fails silently when aria-controls is missing
ai.description: The setupDropdowns function reads the aria-controls attribute from triggers (line 1009) and returns early if the attribute is missing or the referenced element doesn't exist (line 1011). When this happens, the dropdown trigger does not receive the required keyboard event listeners (lines 1035-1049) or aria-expanded management, making the dropdown inaccessible to keyboard and screen reader users. This violates SC 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value).

ai.issueType: Footnote reference aria-label excludes visible link text
ai.description: The footnote reference link (e.g., typically displaying "1" or "[1]") receives an aria-label that replaces the visible text with "Footnote: {content}". The visible number/label of the footnote is not included in the accessible name, violating SC 2.5.3 Label in Name. Speech input users attempting to reference the visible number will not match the accessible name.

ai.issueType: Scroll spy links may not have aria-expanded for expandable navigation pattern
ai.description: The setupScrollSpy function manages aria-current for navigation links (lines 1455, 1461) but if these links control expandable sections or a navigation drawer (common pattern for data-scroll-spy implementations), they lack aria-expanded state management. The code toggles the 'is-active' class and sets aria-current, but if the navigation is collapsible, aria-expanded is required to indicate the visibility state of the controlled content to screen reader users per Success Criterion 4.1.2.

ai.issueType: IntersectionObserver scroll spy does not provide skip mechanism for reduced motion preferences
ai.description: The scroll spy functionality automatically updates navigation states and announces section changes as the user scrolls. Users who have vestibular disorders or motion sensitivity (prefers-reduced-motion) may find automatic announcements based on scroll position disorienting. The code does not check for prefers-reduced-motion media query before enabling the IntersectionObserver or making announcements via CosmosAnnouncer, violating Success Criterion 2.3.3 (Animation from Interactions) and potentially 2.2.2 (Pause, Stop, Hide).

ai.issueType: Highlight function output inserted without HTML validation
ai.description: The highlight() function (lines 1543-1560) returns HTML string with <mark> tags. When this is inserted via innerHTML at line 1658 (${r.snippet}), if the original text contained characters that could break the HTML structure or if the highlight function produces malformed markup, the resulting DOM could be invalid. This affects parsing and could cause assistive technologies to misinterpret the content structure, violating Success Criterion 4.1.1 (Parsing).

ai.issueType: Scroll spy navigation links may lack href or button semantics
ai.description: The code queries for elements with [data-spy-link="${id}"] and treats them as navigation links, setting aria-current and class names. However, if these elements are <a> tags without href attributes or are <span> elements styled as links, they will not be keyboard accessible. The code assumes these are valid links but does not verify they have proper href attributes or role="button" with tabindex and keyboard handlers if they are not anchor tags. This violates Success Criterion 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value).

ai.issueType: aria-activedescendant set to empty string instead of being removed
ai.description: When the active index is -1 (no option selected), the code sets aria-activedescendant to an empty string. This creates an invalid ID reference, failing WCAG 4.1.1 (Parsing) and 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value). Screen readers may not correctly identify which option is active, causing navigation confusion for keyboard users in the search combobox.

ai.issueType: aria-label on generic div without role
ai.description: The div element with class "search-result-tags" has an aria-label attribute but lacks an explicit ARIA role. According to ARIA in HTML specifications, aria-label is not valid on generic div elements without a role. This violates WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value) as the attribute is not supported for this element type, potentially causing screen readers to ignore the label or announce it incorrectly.

ai.issueType: Reply form toggle does not update aria-expanded on trigger button
ai.description: The buildReplyForm function toggles the visibility of the reply form (lines 3110, 3129) but never updates the aria-expanded attribute on the triggering button. Screen readers will not announce the expanded/collapsed state of the reply form, violating WCAG 4.1.2.

ai.issueType: Reply toggle buttons lose accessibility state on dynamic re-render
ai.description: When the comment list is re-rendered after posting a new comment (renderComments), the reply buttons are replaced with new DOM elements. The initialization code that sets aria-expanded and aria-controls only runs once during initial setup, so dynamically added buttons lack these essential accessibility attributes, violating WCAG 4.1.2.

ai.issueType: Keyboard accessibility missing for interactive elements
ai.description: The code contains no event listeners for keyboard interactions (keydown, keyup). If terms are rendered as interactive elements (buttons or links), users cannot navigate or activate them using keyboard-only navigation (Tab, Enter, Space, Escape). This violates WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard and 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value.

ai.issueType: Reduced motion preferences not respected
ai.description: The code contains no CSS or JavaScript to respect prefers-reduced-motion. If this glossary implements smooth scrolling or expand/collapse animations, users with vestibular disorders may experience discomfort. The absence of any media query checks or reduced motion handling violates WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions.

ai.issueType: Duplicate ID values generated when glossary terms start with different non-alphanumeric characters
ai.description: The safeLetter variable strips non-alphanumeric characters and defaults to 'misc'. If terms start with different special characters (e.g., "!" and "@"), both generate safeLetter "misc", causing duplicate id attributes on sections and headings (violating WCAG 4.1.1). This breaks the aria-labelledby relationship on sections and causes navigation links to reference incorrect targets.

ai.issueType: Framework boolean props set invalid ARIA state values
ai.description: The createElement function sets boolean props to an empty string ('') or removes the attribute. For ARIA states (e.g., aria-expanded, aria-hidden), values must be 'true' or 'false'. Setting them to '' or removing them when false breaks programmatic determinability (SC 4.1.2).

ai.issueType: Component re-render hijacks focus unpredictably
ai.description: The _rerender method forces focus to the first focusable element in the new tree whenever the component was previously focused. This disrupts the user's current input position (e.g., typing in a specific field), violating SC 3.2.2 (On Input).

ai.issueType: Router navigation does not move focus to main content
ai.description: The router announces navigation changes via CosmosAnnouncer but does not move keyboard focus to the main content area. Users navigating via keyboard lose their place and must tab through the entire page to find new content, violating SC 2.4.3 (Focus Order).

ai.issueType: Highlight function risks invalid HTML parsing
ai.description: The `highlight` function inserts `<mark>` tags into `text` without escaping existing HTML entities in `text` first. If `text` contains user-generated content with unescaped characters like `<` or `&`, the resulting string may contain broken HTML tags when inserted via `innerHTML`, violating WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.1 (Parsing). Screen readers may fail to parse the content correctly.

ai.issueType: Reduced motion preference checked statically
ai.description: The `reducedMotion` configuration value is evaluated once at module load time using `window.matchMedia(...).matches`. If a user changes their system preference for reduced motion after the page loads, this value will not update, potentially causing JS-controlled animations to continue playing against the user's preference (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.3.3 intent).

ai.issueType: Live region announcement omits new value
ai.description: When a preference is changed, the live region announcement (Line 849) states "Preference saved: [name]" but excludes the actual value selected (e.g., "lg", "dark"). This prevents screen reader users from confirming what the new setting is without navigating away to check the UI, degrading the status notification experience (WCAG 4.1.3).

ai.issueType: Status announcement for navigation open uses incorrect argument type
ai.description: CosmosAnnouncer.announce is called with 'polite' as a string second argument, but the function signature at line 900 expects an options object { assertive = false, delay = 100 }. This causes the announcement options to be ignored, potentially affecting how screen readers announce the navigation open status (WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages).

ai.issueType: Dropdown triggers not establishing aria-controls relationship
ai.description: Dropdown setup reads aria-controls from triggers (line 1009) but never sets it if the attribute is missing from the HTML. Without aria-controls, the programmatic relationship between the trigger button and the controlled menu is not established, violating WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value.

ai.issueType: Dropdown trigger keyboard handler does not check current state before opening
ai.description: The keydown handler on dropdown triggers always calls open() for ArrowDown/ArrowUp/Enter/Space regardless of whether the menu is already open. Expected behavior: when closed, open the menu; when open, ArrowDown/ArrowUp should navigate within the menu. This affects keyboard users (WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard).

ai.issueType: Mobile navigation toggle aria-expanded not initialized on page load
ai.description: The _mobileToggle variable is declared but no initialization code sets its initial aria-expanded state. The openMobileNav/closeMobileNav functions update aria-expanded (lines 977, 997), but the initial state should be set during component initialization for screen readers to understand the toggle's starting state (WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value).

ai.issueType: Keyboard shortcut conflicts with browser functionality
ai.description: The `/` key is commonly used for browser "Find in page". Overriding it without a modifier key (like Alt or Ctrl) violates SC 2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts.

ai.issueType: Informative images may be marked decorative if data attribute missing
ai.description: If `img.dataset.alt` is missing, the code explicitly sets `img.alt` to an empty string (''), marking the image as decorative. If the image is informative (common for lazy-loaded content), this results in missing alternative text (WCAG 1.1.1). The code should not default to empty string without verifying the image is decorative.

ai.issueType: Image fallback logic overwrites decorative alt text
ai.description: The code uses `img.alt || 'Image unavailable'` to set fallback text. This treats an empty string (`alt=""`, used for decorative images) as falsy and overwrites it with "Image unavailable". This forces decorative images to be announced as informative, violating SC 1.1.1.

ai.issueType: Scroll spy selector vulnerable to injection breaking aria-current
ai.description: The `id` from `entry.target.id` is interpolated directly into the CSS selector without escaping. If an ID contains special characters (e.g., quotes), the selector fails, `aria-current` is not updated on the navigation link, and users lose track of their location (SC 4.1.2).

ai.issueType: Scroll spy announcement may be empty
ai.description: If the active link contains no text content (e.g., icon-only), `link.textContent.trim()` returns an empty string. The announcer speaks "Now in section: ", which provides no context to screen reader users (SC 4.1.3).

ai.issueType: Search result tag container aria-label hides visible tag names
ai.description: The `div` containing the tags has `aria-label="Tags"`. This overrides the accessible name of the div, causing the actual tag names (inside the child spans) to be excluded from the parent link's accessible name calculation. Users cannot hear which tags apply to the result (SC 4.1.2).

ai.issueType: Dynamic search results hidden without announcement
ai.description: When the search query is shortened (`q.length < 2`), the results container is hidden (Line 1802) but no status message is announced. Users relying on screen readers are not informed that the results have been cleared, violating WCAG 4.1.3 (Status Messages).

ai.issueType: Accessible planet selection list not initialized
ai.description: The function `setupAccessibleList()` (defined at Line 2026) generates keyboard-accessible buttons for each planet, providing an alternative to the mouse-only canvas interaction. However, this function is never called within the `CosmosBootstrap.register` callback. Consequently, screen reader and keyboard users cannot select planets because the canvas is hidden from the accessibility tree (Line 2066) and the accessible list is never rendered. This violates WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value).

ai.issueType: Interactive canvas hidden from accessibility tree
ai.description: The `_canvas` element is programmed with click and mousemove event listeners (lines 2053, 2060), making it an interactive control for selecting planets. However, line 2066 explicitly sets `aria-hidden="true"`, which removes the element from the accessibility tree. This prevents screen reader users from perceiving or interacting with the canvas functionality, violating WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value).

ai.issueType: Required quiz input missing aria-required attribute
ai.description: The quiz question requires the user to select an answer (enforced by validation logic at Line 2473), but the radiogroup container lacks `aria-required="true"`. Screen reader users are not informed that this input is mandatory before interacting, violating SC 3.3.2.

ai.issueType: Validation error state applied to individual radio inputs instead of radiogroup
ai.description: When no answer is selected, `aria-invalid="true"` is applied to every radio input individually (Line 2476) rather than the `radiogroup` container. This incorrectly implies each option is invalid rather than the selection state being missing. SC 3.3.1 requires the item in error to be identified accurately.

ai.issueType: Lightbox close button label does not match visible text
ai.description: The button has visible text "✕" but the aria-label "Close image viewer" does not include this character. Speech input users saying "click ✕" may fail to match the accessible name (WCAG 2.5.3).

ai.issueType: Lightbox image initial alt text is empty
ai.description: The image element is created with alt="" before showImage() sets the correct value. If the image loads or is accessed by AT before showImage() completes, it may be announced as decorative (WCAG 1.1.1).

ai.issueType: Gallery items missing click event listener
ai.description: Elements are given role="button" but no click listener is attached in this code to trigger the open() function. Mouse users cannot activate the gallery items (WCAG 4.1.2).

ai.issueType: Reading history progress bar values not updated dynamically
ai.description: The updateProgress function saves data but does not call renderHistory(). The progress bar aria-valuenow and visual width in the history list never update after initial load (WCAG 4.1.2).

ai.issueType: Gallery item aria-expanded state never updates to true
ai.description: aria-expanded is initialized to 'false' but because no event listener calls open(), the state never changes to 'true' when the lightbox opens. Screen readers are not informed of the state change (WCAG 4.1.2).

ai.issueType: Newsletter input missing aria-invalid and overwrites aria-describedby
ai.description: When the newsletter form shows an error state, the input field is not marked with aria-invalid="true", failing WCAG 3.3.1. Additionally, setting aria-describedby directly overwrites any existing descriptions (e.g., format hints), failing WCAG 1.3.1. Screen reader users are not informed of the invalid state, and may lose context about the input's expected format.

ai.issueType: Like button action triggers incorrect live region announcement
ai.description: When a user clicks the "Like" button, the page re-renders the comment list and announces "X comments loaded" (Line 3138), which is misleading for a Like action. Similarly, posting a comment triggers both "comments loaded" and "Comment posted successfully", causing redundant announcements. This degrades the experience for screen reader users (WCAG 4.1.3).

ai.issueType: Toast close button visible label not in accessible name
ai.description: The close button has visible text '✕' but the `aria-label` is "Dismiss notification". WCAG 2.5.3 (Label in Name) requires the visible text to be included in the accessible name for speech input users.

ai.issueType: aria-describedby persists after form reset
ai.description: When the form is reset (Line 3369), the `aria-describedby` attribute on the input is not cleared. If the user does not submit again, the input continues to reference a message ID that may be hidden or irrelevant, violating SC 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value).

ai.issueType: aria-busy state not reset if subscription fails
ai.description: Inside the `setTimeout` callback, if `recordSubscription` throws an error, the `aria-busy='false'` reset (Line 3370) is skipped. The form remains in a busy state indefinitely, blocking access for screen reader users (SC 4.1.2).

ai.issueType: Dynamic content load announcement not using aria-live region
ai.description: The CosmosAnnouncer.announce() call at line 4523 announces 'All articles loaded' to users, but this code does not update an element with role="status", role="alert", or aria-live attribute. Screen reader users relying on live regions will not receive this status announcement. This maps to WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.3 (Status Messages).

ai.issueType: Navigation landmark label not unique
ai.description: The `nav` element is given a static `aria-label` ("Glossary alphabet navigation"). If `renderGlossary` is called multiple times (e.g., multiple glossaries on one page), multiple landmarks will share the same accessible name, making them indistinguishable to screen reader users (WCAG 1.3.1, 4.1.2).

ai.issueType: Navigation link href targets non-unique ID
ai.description: The `href` attribute is constructed using a non-unique ID prefix ('glossary-'). If multiple glossary instances exist, links in one instance may jump to sections in another instance, causing navigation errors (WCAG 4.1.1).

ai.issueType: Section ID not scoped to container
ai.description: The `section` ID is generated globally ('glossary-' + safeLetter). Multiple calls to `renderGlossary` will create duplicate IDs in the DOM, violating WCAG 4.1.1 (Parsing) and breaking fragment identifiers.

ai.issueType: ), this reference may point to a heading in a different glossary instance if IDs clash, failing WCAG 4.1.2.
ai.description: Line 4938: section.setAttribute('aria-labelledby', h2.id);

ai.issueType: Jump announcement lacks context for multiple instances
ai.description: The live region announcement ("Jumped to terms starting with...") does not identify which glossary instance was navigated. If multiple glossaries exist, the user cannot distinguish which one was affected (WCAG 4.1.3).

webhint.description: Elements must meet enhanced color contrast ratio thresholds: Element has insufficient color contrast of 5.32 (foreground color: #ffffff, background color: #6b6b6b, font size: 10.0pt (13.3333px), font weight: normal). Expected contrast ratio of 7:1
